claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 went live at 22:00 and changed multi-node order reservation to prioritize east node first
claims.corroboration: Verified source from inventory_control at trust_tier 1
claims.limitation: Does not yet prove causation with held orders

claims.statement: All 186 held orders were routed to east node and flagged as split-reservation exception; reports began at 06:00, approximately 8 hours after v18 went live
claims.corroboration: m8_e10 from customer_support (trust 2, reviewed); m8_e02 from observability (trust 1, verified)
claims.limitation: Temporal correlation is strong but causation not yet confirmed

claims.statement: Allocation rule set v18 may have a defect that causes split-reservation exceptions when reserving from east node for multi-node orders
claims.corroboration: Pattern of split-reservation exceptions on east-node routed orders correlates with v18 deployment
claims.limitation: No diagnostic evidence yet; alternative causes (carrier feed lag, inventory drift) not ruled out

claims.statement: Inventory control reports allocation totals reconcile and nothing looks wrong on inventory side
claims.corroboration: From incident channel (trust 2), does not rule out subtle inventory count issues
claims.limitation: Limited scope check; does not address split-reservation or carrier-side discrepancies

claims.statement: Carrier operations on-call sees nothing obvious on dock schedule
claims.limitation: Does not rule out carrier feed lag; lack of visibility into carrier's own confirmation queue noted in m8_e09

claims.statement: A critical observability gap exists: dashboards cannot show how booked pickups relate to carrier-side confirmation
claims.limitation: Confirms gap exists but does not diagnose whether carrier lag is the actual cause

capability_gaps.capability: Visibility into carrier confirmation queue and pickup acceptance status
capability_gaps.reason: Current dashboards only show order state; cannot correlate booked pickups with carrier's own booking confirmations

next_action.rationale: The split-reservation exception flag on all 186 held orders is the strongest discriminating signal. Auditing allocation exceptions will reveal whether v18's east-node-first logic is generating malformed reservations (indicating allocation_rule_defect) or whether reservations are correct but carriers are not picking them up (indicating carrier_feed_lag). This is the highest-information diagnostic.
next_action.expected_information_gain: Will show whether split-reservation exceptions are structural artifacts of v18's reservation logic or symptoms of downstream carrier problems. Discriminates between allocation_rule_defect and carrier_feed_lag mechanisms.
